claims.statement: The React entrypoint installs theme, React Query, organization-scope invalidation, editor and telemetry setup before rendering the App component.
The SPA uses a browser router inside shared providers, and protects pages through route-level authorization wrappers such as organization-user or platform-admin requirements.
The generated OpenAPI paths type is shared by openapi-fetch and its React Query wrapper; authFetch is retained for endpoints outside the schema.

Client requests ensure token validity, attach CSRF tokens to mutating methods, prefer browser cookies with bearer fallback, and verify session state before treating an arbitrary 401 as an expired session.

Client transient retry logic is limited to 502/503/504 replay-safe methods and explicitly excludes workflow endpoint paths; query and mutation retries are disabled by default in React Query configuration.
The Vite development server proxies API, OpenAPI, MCP, auth, embed, websocket, and object storage routes and rewrites /api/auth to backend /auth.

The React contexts hold cross-route client state such as selected organization scope and branding; OrgScopeProvider persists the selected scope and refreshes branding/terminology after scope changes, while server-side authorization remains authoritative.

The app-code platform compatibility hooks expose workflow operations to embedded apps through a typed execution hook that manages per-execution deferred results, subscriptions, and cleanup; Monaco conflict decorations are local editor support for detecting and reviewing conflict regions.

Shared client component families separate reusable access-level selection, content rendering, route layout and primitive control behavior from product-domain components; the layout and primitive examples are reusable presentation shells and do not implement backend permission checks.

Authentication setup components present passkey or password registration choices through callbacks, while a separate transition screen explains the session-resolution interval after credentials succeed; these components present the flow and do not implement server authentication.

The shared Logo component resolves organization-scoped custom branding, displays a loading placeholder, and falls back to the default logo and product name; the icons family supplies inline vendor marks such as the GitHub SVG.

Shared list controls include offset/limit-based pagination and a controlled debounced SearchBox with immediate clear behavior; QuickAccess delays its form/workflow queries until opened and enables workflow metadata only for platform administrators.

The services UI family receives service records and action callbacks at its list surface and provides a live-log hook that subscribes to a service WebSocket channel, accumulates incoming lines, and unsubscribes during cleanup.

Shared settings rows expose labeled switches and busy states through callbacks, while JsonYamlEditor maintains separate JSON/YAML buffers and does not emit invalid documents; its schema prop is explicitly reserved and not yet wired into Monaco.
Window presentation components provide a reduced-motion-aware maximized overlay and a dock that appears only when minimized-window items exist.

MetricsCardError is a shared metric-card presentation component that renders an alert from a label and normalizes an optional unknown error with a fallback message; it does not establish metric or service health.

HomeBrowse composes type filters, collection context, sorting, view mode, resource renderers, empty states and pagination from parent-provided state and callbacks; ResourceCard/ResourceList provide open and pin callbacks while CatalogFilters provides the type selector.

Home collection navigation delegates selection and CRUD/reorder operations to callbacks and presents an overflow menu; CollectionEditor gathers metadata, scope and resource membership into a parent save payload, while CollectionIconPicker provides searchable icon selection. Collection membership preserves existing resource permissions and does not grant access.
RoleActionsMenu labels a role-specific dropdown and emits edit/delete callbacks; mutations and authorization remain owned by the parent page/API.
